title: menuz's macos.bats fails setup_file on ubuntu-26.04, whose /usr/bin holds a dangling link, so CI's Ubuntu leg is red
body:
## What

menuz's `opt/menuz/test/macos.bats` fails in its `setup_file` on GitHub's ubuntu-26.04 runner image. CI's "Test on Ubuntu" has been red since `ubuntu-latest` moved to that image, and the leg stops before it tests the utilities after menuz.

`setup_file` links every name in `/usr/bin` and `/bin` into `$SYSBIN`, and the first link of a name wins: line 37 skips a name that is already linked, testing `[ -e "$SYSBIN/${f##*/}" ]`. Where `/bin` is `/usr/bin`, the loop meets each name twice, and the second meeting is skipped because `-e` is true for the first link. But `-e` follows the link, so it is false when the link dangles. Then `ln -s` runs a second time, fails because the name is already there, and errexit fails `setup_file`. ubuntu-26.04's `/usr/bin/grub-ntldr-img` is such a link.

## Measured

Read 30 Oct 2026, from GitHub's logs of CI's "Utilz Tests":

- Run 41115734657, the push of 05538ca3: "Test on Ubuntu" is red, on image ubuntu-26.04 (20261025.179.1).
  - Its log has `not ok 1 setup_file failed`, from `setup_file` in macos.bats at line 37, with `ln: failed to create symbolic link '/tmp/bats-run-P3N1KC/file/1/sysbin/grub-ntldr-img': Already exists`.
  - bats then ran menuz.bats' tests 14 to 145, all ok, and warned `Executed 133 instead of expected 145 tests`, so none of macos.bats' 13 tests ran.
  - The job's loop (`utilz test $utility || exit 1`) stopped at menuz, so cleanz, clipz and macoz were not tested.
  - Test Summary is red.
- `[ -e ]` was false for a name that `ln` then found in `$SYSBIN`. Only a link whose target does not resolve gives that, so `/usr/bin/grub-ntldr-img`, the first link's target, dangles on that image.
- Run 40945413129, the push of 5f5ee378 on 29 Oct: green, on image ubuntu-24.04 (20261025.353.1). It tested menuz and then cleanz, clipz and macoz. `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` (`.github/workflows/tests.yml:37`) is the same in both runs, and `git diff 5f5ee378 05538ca3 -- opt/menuz` is empty: the image changed, not menuz.
- Both runs skipped "Test on macOS" and "menuz app (macOS)", because those jobs run only on a tag push or a manual run (`tests.yml:115` and `:528`), so this defect does not skip them. A tag's run tests Ubuntu too, so the next release's Test Summary would also be red.
- The idiom `[ -e ... ] || ln -s` appears once in the tracked tree (`git grep`): macos.bats:37.

## Design

Size: XS.

- Line 37 becomes `[ -e "$SYSBIN/${f##*/}" ] || [ -L "$SYSBIN/${f##*/}" ] || ln -s "$f" "$SYSBIN/${f##*/}"`.
- `-L` is true for a symlink whatever its target, so a dangling first link counts as linked, and the first link of a name still wins.
- A two-line comment above the loop says why and names this issue.
- The change is test-only, so it gets no CHANGELOG line and no menuz VERSION bump, as with 1164c444 and bfd1cdb0.

## Proof

By reading. In bash, `[ -e f ]` follows f's links and is false when they do not resolve. `[ -L f ]` is true for any symlink, whether or not it dangles, and bash 3.2 has it too. With the change, the second meeting of `grub-ntldr-img` finds `-L` true and skips `ln`, so `setup_file` goes on. On Linux and on macOS, a name met once, or met twice with a target that resolves, is linked exactly as before.

The proof in CI is the run after hv's push. "Test on Ubuntu" on ubuntu-26.04 runs macos.bats' 13 tests there for the first time, then cleanz, clipz and macoz. The macOS jobs run only on a tag or a manual run.

Those suites meet ubuntu-26.04 for the first time, so they may find another difference. Its `ln` says `Already exists` where GNU's says `File exists`, which suggests its coreutils are not GNU's.
